# vetr.dev

> Small browser tools. Those listed here can also be driven programmatically: each has one JSON-in, JSON-out function, `submit(request)`, which its web page, a `window.<Name>` object in that page and a command-line script all share. The script runs in plain Node 22 with no install unless its entry says otherwise.

Each entry links the tool's API description: request and result schema, errors, and a worked example.

## Tools with an API

- [Forecast Calibration](https://vetr.dev/forecast-calibration/api.md): compare stated probabilities with binary outcomes; calibration plot against simulated calibrated worlds, Monte Carlo p-values for calibration error and log loss. Page: https://vetr.dev/forecast-calibration/ ; browser: `window.ForecastCalibration` ; CLI: `node forecast-calibration/cli.mjs request.json`
- [Sankey Diagrams](https://vetr.dev/sankey/api.md): Sankey diagrams from data tables (wide, long, link list, crosstab), flow matrices or a saved project; returns the project as JSON, exports SVG, PNG or an R bundle. Page: https://vetr.dev/sankey/ ; browser: `window.SankeyApp` ; CLI: `node sankey/scripts/render.cjs request.json diagram.svg` (not plain Node: it drives headless Chromium through Playwright, so it needs `npm ci` and `npx playwright install chromium` in `sankey/` first; errors are plain text)
- [Text in Image](https://vetr.dev/text-in-image/api.md): write a text inside the shape of an image (PNG pixels in); lines wrapped to the shape, letters coloured from the image, size iterated until the text fills it; returns glyph positions and colours, exports SVG. Page: https://vetr.dev/text-in-image/ ; browser: `window.TextInImage` (its `submit` returns a Promise; it runs in a worker) ; CLI: `node text-in-image/cli.mjs request.json --svg fill.svg` (`image` may be a PNG path there)
- [Crossword Generator](https://vetr.dev/crossword/api.md): crosswords from answers and clues, optionally shaped like a target picture (mask or RGBA pixels; PNG on the CLI); greedy layout then MCMC refinement, scored by the same seven penalty terms as the R generator; returns trimmed grids, numbered across/down entries and the terms, and draws SVG. Page: https://vetr.dev/crossword/ ; browser: `window.Crossword` (its calls return promises, as the page runs the search in a Web Worker) ; CLI: `node crossword/cli.mjs request.json`
- [Raster to Vector](https://vetr.dev/raster-to-vector/api.md): turn a raster image (RGBA pixels in; PNG on the CLI) into an SVG of flat-colour regions with smooth outlines; weighted k-means colours with k by Davies-Bouldin, marching-squares or original tracer, wavelet / Fourier / Hadamard smoothing, containment paint order; same SVG as the R version for the same request; returns palette, regions in paint order and the SVG. Page: https://vetr.dev/raster-to-vector/ ; browser: `window.RasterToVector` (its `submit` returns a Promise; it runs in a worker) ; CLI: `node raster-to-vector/cli.mjs --image in.png --svg out.svg` or `node raster-to-vector/cli.mjs request.json`
- [Statistical Intuitions](https://vetr.dev/intuitions/api.md): a gallery of interactive figures, one statistical idea each, behind one `submit({entry, params})` that returns `{entry, params, result}`; entries `zscore-outliers` (pooled vs stratified z-score outlier removal for two normal groups: exact share of each group removed by each rule, and a sweep over one parameter), `threshold-model` (discrete traits from a hidden normal liability: category and contingency-table probabilities, seeded samples, and the two-step polychoric fit of a table), `correlation-geometry` (correlations as angles between unit arrows: the cone of fixed correlation, the cosine-rule range of a third correlation, the equicorrelation and one-pair-at-0 limits, and the feasible interval of one entry of a PSD correlation matrix given the rest, with expected interval widths), `typical-set` (where the probability mass is: the chi distribution as density × volume with its shell and ball masses, the cube criterion for six families against seeded sampled radii, highest-density regions of 1-D mixtures at a water level, and the Beta-type marginal of a uniform point on the sphere) `dag-adjustment` (linear-Gaussian causal graphs, preset or given: the regression coefficient of an adjustment set against the causal effect, the adjustment criterion, every path open or blocked, every candidate set, the front-door estimate, seeded samples, and R² and the induced partial correlation when conditioning on many colliders), `null-pvalues` (ways to break a p-value: under a true null, the p-value histogram, the share below every threshold and the realised false-positive rate at α of a shortcut beside a sound analysis, in seven scenarios, exact or seeded Monte Carlo: batch regressed out first, covariates residualised one at a time, a t-test on bootstrap means, autocorrelated series, two-step filtering, ignored pairing, and hypergeometric pathway tests kept only where a pathway has a hit) `marchenko-pastur` (how many principal components are noise: sample-covariance eigenvalues of seeded noise against the Marchenko–Pastur law, spiked covariances and the BBP threshold for eigenvalues and eigenvector overlaps, and the first principal components of a batch-and-factors model before and after batch correction), `trait-evolution` (traits on a phylogeny, a seeded Yule tree or Newick: one trait along every branch under Brownian motion, a trend, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck, early or late burst, a mid-tree burst or a clade shift to a second optimum, with each lineage's mean and SD; two traits under a rate matrix; and the Brownian bridge between fixed ends by midpoints, kept in a region by stagewise or whole-path rejection) and `tree-covariance` (a tree as the tips' Brownian-motion covariance: shared paths, tips as arrows and seeded tip values; re-rooting with the restricted and ordinary likelihoods; and Felsenstein's pruning step by step, one to four traits, against the direct normal likelihood). Page: https://vetr.dev/intuitions/ ; browser: `window.Intuitions` on every gallery page ; CLI: `node intuitions/cli.mjs request.json`
- [Name Tags](https://vetr.dev/name-tags/api.md): lay out names, one per tag, in the cells of a laser-cut tray (a preset, a regular grid or explicit cell centres); each two-line name is fitted around a decoration (DNA helix, Hershey script with an EKG trace, or none) by BFGS with restarts, as the R version does with the same seeds, or a sheet of logos is drawn instead; returns the fits and one SVG per tray-full at 96 units per inch. Page: https://vetr.dev/name-tags/ ; browser: `window.NameTags` (its calls return promises, as the page fits in a Web Worker) ; CLI: `node name-tags/cli.mjs request.json --out dir` (names, tray and logos may be file paths there)
- [Table Seating](https://vetr.dev/seating/api.md): seat guests at tables (seats per table, or a list of tables with capacities and room positions) to maximize how alike each table's guests are by category, pair scores and a geography term that pushes chosen guests to far-apart tables, with must-sit-together and must-sit-apart constraints; a fixed-temperature Barker swap chain that keeps the best seating, the same chain as the R version for the same seed; returns the best seating, its terms, broken constraints, a score trace and optionally every accepted move. Page: https://vetr.dev/seating/ ; browser: `window.Seating` (its `submit` returns a Promise; it runs in a worker) ; CLI: `node seating/cli.mjs request.json` (it also reads the R version's request spelling)
- [Hypercube Rotation](https://vetr.dev/hypercube/api.md): one frame of a rigid k-cube's rotating shadow (k = 3 to 9), unfolding from a line through every dimension and folding back, replayed from trajectories solved by the R pipeline (NikVetr/shape_rotation); returns the frame as SVG, or its projected vertices, faces in painting order with depth, colour and dimension numeral, and edges; translucent (R's base renderer) or opaque lit faces (R's RGL renderer), a turnable camera, light or dark. Page: https://vetr.dev/hypercube/ ; browser: `window.Hypercube` (its `submit` returns a Promise, as the page loads plans on demand) ; CLI: `node hypercube/cli.mjs request.json` (`--frames 1-1448:2 --out dir` writes SVG frame sequences)
- [Photomosaic](https://vetr.dev/photomosaic/api.md): arrange photos into a grid that reproduces a target picture from a distance; the target's pixels (RGBA, base64) and each photo's average colour in, the photo for each cell out, each photo used once (or up to maxUses) by an exact Hungarian assignment on the R script's HSL cost (or CIELAB), with the R script's grid rule, ImageMagick's scaling arithmetic and R's shuffle for the same seed; returns the assignment, per-cell costs and the target's cell colours. Page: https://vetr.dev/photomosaic/ ; browser: `window.Photomosaic` (its `submit` returns a Promise; it runs in a worker) ; CLI: `node photomosaic/cli.mjs --target target.png --photos folder/ --png mosaic.png` (PNG and JPEG files) or `node photomosaic/cli.mjs request.json`
- [Signature Correction](https://vetr.dev/signature/api.md): clean up a signature drawn with a trackpad, mouse, stylus or finger (strokes with optional time and pressure, CSV, a 2 × n matrix or SVG paths in); arc-length resampling, Fourier smoothing over each stroke and wavelet (MODWT) smoothing that can be scaled region by region, pen widths from smoothed signing speed or, without timing, from curvature by the two-thirds power law, or from pressure; returns the corrected strokes with widths, their unioned filled outline and a transparent SVG; optionally morphs it into a second signature (the R script's wavelet-coefficient interpolation, all strokes paired). Page: https://vetr.dev/signature/ ; browser: `window.Signature` (also `exportPngBlob` for a transparent PNG) ; CLI: `node signature/cli.mjs request.json --svg out.svg` (or a `.csv` / `.svg` file in place of the request; `--frames dir` writes the morph frames)
- [Message Collage](https://vetr.dev/message-collage/api.md): lay out short messages (farewell or thank-you notes) as one dense collage card; each message draws a bundled font family, style and relative size, one global scale sets the text, lines flow into the free cells of an occupancy grid (the card grows downward), colours avoid nearby messages, and the best of N seeded layouts by empty space is kept, exactly as the R version does for the same request and fonts; returns every line's text, cells, position in inches, font, size and colour, the card size and empty fraction, and every run's score; exports SVG (outlined or selectable text), PDF and, in the page, PNG. Page: https://vetr.dev/message-collage/ ; browser: `window.MessageCollage` (its calls return promises; it runs in a worker) ; CLI: `node message-collage/cli.mjs request.json --svg card.svg` (or `--messages notes.txt`, one message per line)
- [Helix and Braid](https://vetr.dev/helix/api.md): parametric DNA double helices (R's draw_DNA: turns, start angle, amplitude, frequency, phase between the strands for grooves, square-wave shape, depth-shaded strand widths, a crossing gap that shows which strand passes in front, base pairs per turn with gap, thickness and alternating sides, a straight extension of one or both strands, rotation, a box to fit or stretch into, three colours) and braided multi-strand lines (R's braid_segment: k coloured strands, twists of either hand, width, length, rotation, cut wherever strands swap depth and painted back to front), checked against R; returns the SVG, filled, as cutting outlines of what can be seen, or as centrelines, in mm, in or px, and the geometry: the helix's visible strand pieces with widths and its base pairs, or the braid's cuts, depth order per segment and every crossing's over and under strand. Page: https://vetr.dev/helix/ ; browser: `window.Helix` (also `exportPngBlob`) ; CLI: `node helix/cli.mjs request.json --svg out.svg`
